phase: ARS-RH Phase 3 — Sigma^2 number-variance: the orthogonal long-range witness for the Phase-1 finite-height residual
section_0_anti_claim: BINDING. This measures whether an INDEPENDENT long-range statistic (Sigma^2 number variance) resolves the same finite-height structure the r-tilde leg found. It is an instrument-corroboration test, NOT evidence about RH. A measured rigidity is a property of the finite-height zero window and the estimator, not of the Riemann hypothesis.
why_this_phase: Every Phase-1/2 result lives in the r-tilde family (matched-density null, flow control, sigma-shape) — one SHORT-RANGE adjacent-gap statistic read through multiple clever nulls. That single-statistic dependence, not the single-window 2.4sigma, is the real fragility. Sigma^2(L) is orthogonal in mechanism: LONG-range rigidity, a different aspect of the same spectrum. If it shows the low-gamma excess too, Phase 1 goes from 'one statistic well-nulled' to 'two mechanistically-independent statistics agree.' If it is clean where r-tilde showed 2.4sigma, that is ALSO substantive: the residual is a short-range effect invisible to long-range rigidity, which characterizes what KIND of structure it is.

blocking_prerequisite_decoy_battery.rule: The Sigma^2 verdict on zeta is read ONLY AFTER the GENERAL (empirical, data-driven) unfolding passes a known-answer decoy battery. The theta-exact Riemann-von Mangoldt unfolding is zeta-SPECIFIC and analytic — clean for zeta precisely because it is bespoke — so it must NOT be the general path, or the tool only works on the one substrate whose answer we already know. General empirical unfolding is what would be used on Maass/neural data; it must be proven to have power BEFORE its zeta verdict is trusted.
blocking_prerequisite_decoy_battery.the_specific_trap: An over-flexible empirical unfolding absorbs real long-range fluctuations into the 'smooth' density -> SUPPRESSES Sigma^2 -> reads FALSELY RIGID. That would make zeta look rigid for a reason having nothing to do with zeta. The Poisson decoy is the sentinel: over-smoothing shows up as Poisson Sigma^2(L) coming out BELOW L.
gate_conditions: POISSON decoy under general unfolding -> Sigma^2(L) ~ L (linear, no false rigidity). If suppressed below L, the unfolding over-smooths -> ABORT and reduce flexibility.
GUE decoy under general unfolding -> Sigma^2(L) ~ (1/pi^2)(ln(2 pi L) + gamma_E + 1) (log-rigidity recovered, neither inflated nor suppressed).

A SUPER-RIGID decoy (rigidity beyond GUE) under general unfolding -> Sigma^2(L) BELOW the GUE curve. Proves the instrument can SEE extra rigidity of the kind sought in zeta (the 'approach from above').
blocking_prerequisite_decoy_battery.only_if_all_pass: read the zeta Sigma^2 verdict. Cross-check the general path against the theta-exact R-vM unfolding on zeta as a zeta-ONLY ground-truth (general must reproduce theta-exact); disagreement means the general unfolding is the story, not zeta.

sealed_prediction.sensitivity_prior_SHIFTED_UP: Per sensitivity_specificity_decouple: the instrument (decoy-gated) WILL have power to resolve a long-range rigidity difference at low-gamma if one exists. My prior that it resolves is shifted up — this substrate has beaten my conservative sensitivity call 3-for-3.
sealed_prediction.specificity_prior_HELD_FIXED: Whether zeta low-gamma actually shows Sigma^2 EXCESS rigidity (curve BELOW GUE) versus sits ON GUE is the open question, and I do NOT couple 'the instrument is sensitive' to 'it will confirm.' The decoy gate is the specificity guarantee; a null must be one the estimator provably could have shown non-null.
sealed_prediction.substantive_point_estimate: r-tilde is an ADJACENT-gap statistic, so the finite-height residual it found is short-range-weighted. Conservative call: the low-gamma Sigma^2 excess (rigidity below GUE) will be WEAKER than the 2.4sigma r-tilde margin, possibly sub-detection at moderate L, because the 'approach to GUE from above' is concentrated at the nearest-neighbour scale.
sealed_prediction.explicit_pessimism_flag: This conservative 'short-range only' call is EXACTLY the direction I have been wrong 3-for-3 (all conservative on sensitivity). The decoupling correction says lean toward 'Sigma^2 shows it too.' I record the conservative point estimate AND the correction; if Sigma^2 shows clear excess, that is the pattern continuing, not a surprise to explain away.

both_outcomes_precommitted_substantive.agree_excess: zeta Sigma^2 below GUE at low gamma, clean at high gamma -> Phase 1 CORROBORATED by an orthogonal statistic; two mechanistically-independent legs. The residual is a genuine multi-scale rigidity excess.
both_outcomes_precommitted_substantive.clean: zeta Sigma^2 on GUE at low gamma where r-tilde showed 2.4sigma -> the residual is characterized as SHORT-RANGE (nearest-neighbour only), invisible to long-range rigidity. Substantive: it tells us the kind of structure, and it BOUNDS the r-tilde leg to the short-range scale.

sealed_prediction.not_a_win_lose: This is a CHARACTER measurement, not a test I pass. Both outcomes inform; neither is failure. Designed so sensitivity cannot buy the answer and either result is a finding.

method_commitments.statistic: Sigma^2(L) = Var_a( N[a, a+L] ) over unit-mean-spacing unfolded levels, averaged over window starts a across the spectrum interior.
method_commitments.general_unfolding: empirical: smooth polynomial (order calibrated BY the decoy battery to reproduce Poisson=L and GUE=analytic simultaneously) fit to the cumulative staircase N(x); xi_i = N_smooth(x_i).
method_commitments.theta_exact_unfolding: zeta-only ground-truth: xi_i = Riemann-von Mangoldt N(gamma_i). Used ONLY to cross-check the general path on zeta, never as the general estimator.
method_commitments.L_range: moderate L (e.g. 1..40) where GUE log-rigidity is clearly separated from Poisson linear and finite-N saturation is not yet dominant.
method_commitments.windows: low-gamma zeta block (steep finite-height deviation) + high-gamma block (flat control), same as Phase 1.
method_commitments.error_bars: GUE ensemble (Dumitriu-Edelman tridiagonal) realizations give the Sigma^2(L) jitter band; zeta excess judged against that band.
